title: Incident response plan and severity model
status_rationale: SOC2-026 requires documented detection, triage, containment, remediation, communication and lessons learned; UNB-GAP-034 and UNB-OPS-001 call for cyber incident response; no plan exists. The business plan section on incident learning is a draft governance position, not a plan.
target_answer: An approved incident response plan aligned with NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3 and CSF 2.0 covers detection, triage, containment, eradication, recovery and post-incident review; defines security incident, privacy breach and outage and how one event can trigger several obligations; uses a severity model that drives escalation and notification; includes playbooks for unauthorized grant or payment instructions, tenant data exposure, compromised AI agent, compromised build pipeline, credential compromise and ransomware; is reviewed annually; and a summary is shared with customers.
current_practice: No incident response plan exists. Not established.
intended_practice: Write and approve the plan before any customer production data is loaded.
customer_statement: Echelon does not yet have an adopted incident response plan; one will be established before Unbound handles customer production data.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)
open_questions: Who will approve the incident response plan for Echelon Foundry, LLC?

title: Incident response roles, on-call coverage and external support
status_rationale: Headcount, named security officer and retainers are not established (current-state brief). No cyber insurance is established.
target_answer: A named incident commander and at least one trained deputy, 24x7 paging with escalation (achievable only with a second trained responder or a contracted MDR or incident response provider), a retained incident response and forensics firm, outside breach counsel, and a verified customer contact registry; AI agents may gather evidence and draft communications but may not send regulatory or customer notices, release holds or destroy evidence without human approval.
current_practice: Unknown; no evidence located. No named security officer, retainer or insurance located. Current position (2026-11-25): Echelon has one principal, the managing member, and no staff, on-call rotation or contracted support provider, so this commitment cannot be met today.
intended_practice: Assign roles and contract a retainer before production.
customer_statement: Incident response roles and external support have not yet been established.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)
open_questions: Will Echelon retain an incident response firm and breach counsel, and when?
Will Echelon obtain cyber insurance (see INS)?

challenge.contractually_required: Customers ask for named contacts and 24x7 escalation.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Automated containment reduces the human actions needed in the first hour.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Pre-authorized automated containment; paging with escalation.
challenge.continuous_evidence: On-call schedule coverage report; drill timings.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Automated first-hour containment plus a retained incident response firm on contract for surge capacity and independence.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Partially: retainer contract and drill timing records.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.alternative_risks: Retained firm lacks system familiarity unless onboarded.
supporting_arguments: A retainer converts key-person risk into a contractual capability.

title: Incident response testing and exercises
status_rationale: SOC2-015 requires dated evidence of incident response tabletop exercises; none has been held.
target_answer: Annual tabletop exercises covering ransomware, insider misuse, compromised AI agent, cross-tenant exposure and an incident during year-end giving peaks, with customer participation offered; semiannual automated technical drills measuring time to retrieve logs, disable accounts, place a sponsor-policy hold, revoke agent credentials and rotate keys; corrective actions tracked to closure and summaries shared.
intended_practice: Hold the first tabletop when the plan is approved.

challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Annual discussion-based tabletops test coordination but not technical capability; findings are often not tracked to closure.
challenge.legally_required: Not for Echelon directly; NYDFS 500.16 and PCI DSS 12.10.2 require testing for covered entities.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Scheduled technical drills (restore, revoke, hold, kill switch) run automatically in a non-production cell with timing captured.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Drill timing records and corrective action aging.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Annual tabletop for decisions and communications plus frequent automated technical drills measuring time to contain.

supporting_arguments: Measured technical response time is more informative than attendance at a tabletop.

title: Customer incident notification commitments
status_rationale: REQ-X-016 requires incident records to define earliest credible compromise and independent channels; UNB-XIN-IAM-005 requires tenant notification of break-glass within 1 hour; CNV-PLT-007 requires immediate notice of platform holds. No general customer breach notice commitment exists.
target_answer: Initial notice to affected customers within 24 hours of reasonable suspicion that customer data or covered services are affected, with updates at least every 24 hours until containment and a final report; the clock starts at reasonable suspicion, not confirmation; notices include what is known, affected data and tenants, actions taken, recommended customer actions and contact; notices are sent to registered contacts and confirmed over a second authenticated channel; subprocessor incidents and incidents affecting shared infrastructure or the same release are included. This trigger is the single definition used in contract terms (ANS-LEG-003); regulatory clocks for bank (ANS-IR-005) and securities customers run in addition, and the shortest applicable deadline governs.
intended_practice: Adopt in the security addendum after counsel review.
customer_statement: Customer incident notification terms have not yet been adopted; Echelon will propose specific timelines in its security addendum.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

challenge.customer_intent: Learn about incidents fast enough to meet the customer's own legal deadlines and protect its clients.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Customer misses regulatory deadlines or learns of an incident from the press.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Fixed-hour contractual clauses (for example 24, 48 or 72 hours) vary by customer and are measured from ambiguous triggers; vendors often delay notice until confirmation.
challenge.legally_required: Yes in part: the CIRN rule requires bank service providers to notify affected banking organizations as soon as possible for qualifying disruptions; amended Regulation S-P requires covered institutions to ensure service providers notify within 72 hours of becoming aware of a breach; state laws require service providers to notify data owners.
challenge.historical_convention: Notice within 24 to 72 hours of discovery or confirmation.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Obligation matrix computes the earliest applicable deadline per customer at incident declaration.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Notification log with deadline and sent timestamps.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Single uniform early-notice commitment (initial notice within 24 hours of reasonable suspicion affecting customer data or covered services, with updates every 24 hours), satisfying the strictest common obligation, plus structured follow-up data packages.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Very small team cannot staff 24-hour notice; law enforcement delay requests.
challenge.alternative_risks: Early notices on suspicion may later prove false alarms and cause customer burden.
supporting_arguments: Customers' own deadlines (36 hours for banks under CIRN, 72 hours under NYDFS) require earlier vendor notice.
agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Likely; uniform early notice is generally welcomed.'; institutional acceptance rating 'likely' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Counsel may prefer flexible 'without undue delay' language to limit liability.

Institutional acceptance is unvalidated: no buyer, auditor, regulator or insurer evidence or cited source supports an acceptance rating (DD-VAL-ADV-001, DD-VAL-ADV-002). Treat any rating as agent judgment until target-customer conversations or a sourced document support it.

history.change: BL-021: set institutional_acceptance to unknown (prior 'likely' was unsourced agent judgment, kept in supporting_arguments) and added an unvalidated-acceptance note to opposing_arguments (OBJ-VRM-019, OBJ-SKEPTIC-014).
BL-021: declared this the single notification trigger shared with ANS-LEG-003 (OBJ-BANKCISO-012).

title: Bank service provider notification under the 2021 Computer-Security Incident Notification rule
status_rationale: Whether Unbound's customers will include banking organizations, and whether Echelon will perform covered services subject to the Bank Service Company Act, is not established. No Echelon source addresses the rule.
target_answer: Where Echelon provides services to a banking organization subject to the Bank Service Company Act, it notifies each affected bank customer's designated contacts as soon as possible after determining that a computer-security incident has materially disrupted or degraded, or is reasonably likely to materially disrupt or degrade, covered services for four or more hours, and supports the bank's own 36-hour determination and notification to its primary federal regulator with rapid, structured facts. Scheduled maintenance previously communicated is excluded as the rule provides. Designated contacts are collected at onboarding and verified. If a bank customer has not designated a contact, Echelon notifies the bank's chief executive officer and chief information officer, or two individuals with comparable responsibilities, as the rule provides; bank tenant activation requires verified designated contacts.
intended_practice: Determine applicability with counsel and build into the obligation matrix.
customer_statement: Echelon has not yet established a process for bank service provider incident notification; applicability depends on the customer and services, and will be determined with counsel.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)
open_questions: Will any Unbound customer be a banking organization (for example a bank or trust company acting as or for a DAF sponsor)?
Does Unbound constitute covered services under the Bank Service Company Act?

history.change: BL-021: added the CEO and CIO default-contact fallback under the 2021 bank service provider notification rule (OBJ-REGULATOR-003).

title: Service provider notice under amended SEC Regulation S-P (2024)
status_rationale: Applicability depends on whether customers are covered institutions (broker-dealers, registered investment advisers, investment companies, transfer agents). Wealth managers serving DAF donors may be. No Echelon source addresses Regulation S-P.
target_answer: For covered-institution customers, Echelon contractually agrees to take appropriate measures to protect against unauthorized access to customer information and to notify the covered institution as soon as possible and no later than 72 hours after becoming aware of a breach resulting in unauthorized access to a customer information system Echelon maintains; provides structured facts on sensitive customer information affected so the customer can meet its 30-day individual notification deadline; and supports the customer's service provider due diligence and monitoring.
intended_practice: Determine customer types and adopt contract terms with counsel.
customer_statement: Echelon has not yet adopted Regulation S-P service provider terms; it intends to meet the 72-hour service provider notice expectation for covered-institution customers.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)
open_questions: Will Unbound serve SEC-registered advisers or broker-dealers, or DAF sponsors affiliated with them?

title: Forensics, evidence preservation and regulator cooperation
status_rationale: REQ-X-016 requires incident records to define earliest credible compromise, lookback and evidence provenance; SOC2-006 directs protected evidence storage and legal hold; no forensic capability exists.
target_answer: On declaration, logs, snapshots, images and agent ledgers in scope are preserved with hashes and chain of custody under legal hold for at least the longer of seven years or the applicable hold; customers' forensic firms may participate under coordination; Echelon cooperates with customers' regulators, auditors and law enforcement and provides records within agreed timeframes; forensic summaries are shared with affected customers.
intended_practice: Define preservation procedures with the logging architecture.
customer_statement: Forensic preservation and regulator cooperation procedures are planned; not established.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)
open_questions: Is seven years appropriate for incident evidence, aligned with REQ-X-036, or should counsel set a different period?

title: Post-incident review and lessons learned
status_rationale: SOC2-026 requires lessons learned; Tutela requires incidents to feed threats, invariants and regression evidence (tutela@476dc682:requirements/TUTELA-REQUIREMENTS.md TUT-1303); the business plan describes incident learning as a draft governance position.
target_answer: Every significant incident yields a blameless root cause analysis within 10 business days, a customer-facing post-incident report within 15 business days, corrective actions tracked to verified completion, and updates to threat models, invariants, regression tests and detections.
intended_practice: Apply Tutela incident ingestion once Unbound operates.
customer_statement: Post-incident review practices are planned; no incidents have been handled for a production Echelon service.

title: Ransomware preparedness and ransom payment policy
status_rationale: UNB-GAP-034 calls for cyber incident response, immutable backup and restoration tests; no backup or ransom policy exists.
target_answer: Backups are immutable or logically isolated from production and administrative credentials and are restore-tested quarterly; the plan assumes no ransom payment, and any extortion decision requires counsel, insurer (if any) and sanctions screening against OFAC lists, with law enforcement engagement; customers are informed promptly of any data theft or extortion threat involving their data.
customer_statement: Ransomware preparedness is planned; Unbound has no production data to protect yet.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Containment: credential revocation, tenant isolation, platform holds and AI agent kill switch
status_rationale: CNV-PLT-007 defines sponsor-adopted, time-bounded platform holds that never move funds and notify the sponsor immediately; UNB-XIN-IAM-005 defines break-glass limits; SOC2-017 requires agents to be interruptible; none implemented.
target_answer: Pre-authorized containment actions execute within minutes: revoke workforce, service and agent credentials; isolate a tenant; place platform holds under the sponsor's adopted hold policy that never move, reverse or redirect funds and leave the sponsor able to pay through its own bank; stop all or specific AI agents and review every action they took in the affected window from the agent ledger.
intended_practice: Implement with identity, hold policy and agent runtime.
customer_statement: Containment capabilities, including sponsor-policy holds and AI agent stop controls, are specified for Unbound; not implemented.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)
